title: JANUS Engine R0C — Three-State Sorbent Carousel
goal: Test whether multiple annular sorbent sections can provide quasi-continuous service by operating in staggered CAPTURE, REGENERATION and COOLING states while nitrogen is cascaded through cooling, regeneration and inert-service duties.

state_A.name: CAPTURE
state_A.role: Active sorption / purification duty on the selected process stream until the declared breakthrough criterion is reached.

state_B.name: REGENERATION
state_B.role: Restore sorbent working capacity by controlled purge and/or thermal regeneration. Nitrogen is a candidate purge medium where chemically and materially appropriate.

state_C.name: COOLING
state_C.role: Return the regenerated sorbent to its required capture temperature before it is placed back on stream.

architecture.rotation_logic: R1: CAPTURE -> REGENERATION -> COOLING -> CAPTURE; R2 and R3 follow the same cycle with phase offsets so one section may remain available for capture while the others regenerate and cool.
architecture.switching: Functional state switching should be accomplished by controlled flow routing and valves; physical ring rotation is a separate geometric option and is not required for the three-state thermodynamic cycle.

nitrogen_cascade_hypothesis.principle: Do not treat separated N2 as a single-use waste stream if useful temperature, pressure or inerting capacity remains.
candidate_sequence: cold N2 cools the regenerated sorbent section
warmer N2 may then serve as regeneration purge where conditions permit
remaining N2 may serve as an inert barrier or purge between oxygen-rich and hot/mechanical regions
only after useful duties are exhausted is the stream vented, recycled or otherwise dispositioned
nitrogen_cascade_hypothesis.hard_boundary: Nitrogen does not generate refrigeration merely by being nitrogen. Sub-ambient cooling requires a real refrigeration/expansion process or another colder source, and the energy cost must be included in the balance.

minimum_measurements: sorbent identity and mass per ring

timing_model.continuous_service_condition: The number of phased sections and their cycle timing must provide at least one capture-ready section over the intended duty cycle, including switching margin.
timing_model.first_three_section_test: Evaluate whether tau_capture, tau_regen and tau_cool can be scheduled with three phase-offset sections without unacceptable gaps or oversizing.

required_terms: rotational power if the physical ring is rotating
energy_accounting.optimization_objective: Maximize useful sequential duties obtained from each separated stream before disposal while minimizing exergy destruction and auxiliary power.

success_metrics.primary: Repeated CAPTURE -> REGENERATION -> COOLING operation with recoverable sorbent capacity and no process interruption beyond the declared switching tolerance.
secondary: net energy cost per unit of useful purified gas
fraction of N2 exergy used before vent or recycle

failure_modes_to_watch: regeneration slower than capture causing unavoidable service gaps
cooling duty exceeds available cold-N2 capacity
sorbent degrades or loses working capacity
water or CO2 freezes in cold passages
pressure drop dominates useful process gain
cross-contamination between oxygen-rich and regeneration streams
thermal cycling damages seals or annular structure
next_gate: R0C1_SORBENT_AND_DUTY_FREEZE: select one sorbent, one contaminant-removal duty, one annular geometry and one N2 service-flow envelope; then measure tau_capture, tau_regen, tau_cool and full energy balance before coupling to oxygen liquefaction or an engine core.
